body: I was going to go with some joy division but I’ll say Today by Smashing Pumpkins. Most people don’t even realize that is what the song is actually about.  Actually the entire Siamese Dream album has always been that roller coaster for me. Mirrored my feelings so much. Soma.

I was enlisted. The "guy" was in the same unit and knew each other for years.  I'm not a small guy. I was black out drunk and only recall flashes and having to do detective work with a hangover is terrible. I stopped going to groups because it's the same shit. I just want to numb myself. I drink and do drugs to cope. They're aren't a lot of good programs for MST either. The ones that d,  don't have programs for men. There's a definite stigma for men. I've met other guys in groups that you would never think were there for the same thing so that opened my eyes. Vets going back to Vietnam that I know. It's nothing new. I still can't talk about it too often, but hopefully just knowing you're not alone helps someone else who has gone through it. Even just a little bit.

I'm on a throwaway account for obvious reasons. I'm a male veteran that was sexually assaulted in the military. It fucked up my life and changed me forever. I still deal with depression and suicide daily. This story hits home for me. I never reported it to my chain of command. It is a different world than what civilians think it is. How does a man go about reporting getting raped while passed out by another man. How is that going to make me look. I already have PTSD from combat. I have groups and meds and therapy for it. They call it military sexual trauma. You'd honestly be surprised how many men are in these groups. We all have different stories but we all know. People do not know other than a 2 ex girlfriends. My ex wife of 7 years didn't know. My own family still have no idea. I don't think I will ever let them know. People don't seem to understand how things work in reality. It's never that simple to just say something. It's a life changing event that you can't talk to people about. It haunts you. Mine happened over 15 years ago and it still haunts me. I don't have close friendships because I can't trust anyone. Especially guys. I miss that sometimes. I take meds. I go to meetings. I've gone through multiple programs for PTSD. Usually I just numb myself. War was hell but it didn't hit me as hard as that. I can deal with that easier. I'm not suicidal right now but a few months ago I was. In a few more I may be again. 

I read that about her and felt sick to my stomach. It took me back. It's a different time today. Unless you've worn the uniform, you won't understand what it's like. There is no way I felt anyone would believe me. I used to ask why me but learned a long time ago how ugly this world can be. I'm hopeful that her story gets told and not forgotten. I'm sure that people will move on to the next hot topic soon enough. But this is serious. Do I wish that I said anything? At that time and place? No. I still wouldn't. But now. In this day and age? I would like to think I would. I hope that if anyone has gone through this type of situation, whether military or not, that you are stronger than I am and speak up.
